title: After a tier is renamed the details show the old and current name
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit', 'Work Orders — Order Parts' and 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit'.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses, named for example Fleet.
  • Have a new matrix for this test, matrix A, pricing a new category made for this test, category A, with one range from $0.00: Default Markup % 50, tier A Markup % 20.
  • Have a new inventory part for this test, part A, in category A, cost $10.00, in a bin (for example E-11).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, on tier A for work orders.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, with part A added (sold at $12.00: $10.00 × 1.20).
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Click the Tiers tab on Settings › Pricing.
  2. Click tier A's row on the Tiers list.
  3. Click the tier name at the top of the page.
  4. Type a new name (for example Fleet Plus).
  5. Press Enter.
  6. Open work order 1.
  7. Click the Parts tab.
  8. Point at part A's Priced by.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Tiers list shows tier A.

Step 2:

  • Tier A's page opens.

Step 3:

  • The name becomes editable.

Step 4:

  • The new name shows.

Step 5:

  • The title shows the new name.

Step 6:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 7:

  • Part A's Priced by reads the new name (for example Fleet Plus).

Step 8:

  • The details read the old name followed by "(now" and the new name ")" (for example "Fleet (now Fleet Plus)").
  • Part A still sells at $12.00.
